_experiment.description: Stupidity point mapping. Steps set to 2160 = total number of prunable weight entries (196*10 + 10*10 + 10*10) to drive the network toward complete sparsity. The stupidity point is defined formally in ch_proofs (sec_proof_stupidity) as the step at which the adjustment step can no longer compensate for any further removal — i.e., where d_manifold begins growing monotonically and accuracy collapses irreversibly. The experiment provides the empirical evidence for the formal result. The exact step of collapse, the shape of d_manifold just before it, and which layer loses its last weight are all reportable quantities.
literature: Thesis sec_proof_stupidity: formal definition and proof of the stupidity point — this experiment is the empirical counterpart
LeCun et al. 1989 (OBD): notes that pruning beyond a certain saliency threshold degrades accuracy catastrophically — the stupidity point is the manifold-metric analogue of that threshold
